Transfer Policy for Commissioners’ Cadre in EPFO 2025 
 
1. IntroducƟon & General Principles  
 
1.1. 
This policy may be called “Transfer Policy for Commissioners’ Cadre, 2025” hereinaŌer, 
referred to as TP-CC 2025. It shall be applicable to all Commissioners as menƟoned 
under SecƟon 5D(3) of the EPF & MP Act 1952. 
1.2. 
This policy supersedes all earlier policies in this regard. 
1.3. 
The Policy is in response to the direcƟon of the Supreme Court of India as contained 
in the Writ PeƟƟon (Civil) No.82 of 2011(T.S.R Subramanian & ORS. Vs. Union of India 
& Ors. Judgement dated 31.10.2013) and the communicaƟons from the Department 
of Personnel & Training bearing number 11013/10/2013-EsƩ.A dated December 26, 
2013 and January 09, 2014. 
1.4. 
The policy borrows various provisions and contours from DOPT & previous policies 
applicable in EPFO. 
1.5. 
All transfer and posƟngs of Commissioners shall be approved by the Competent 
Authority in accordance with the instant TP-CC 2025. The Competent Authority will be 
advised by the recommendatory body called “Commissioners’ Transfer & Placement 
CommiƩee” (CTPC). 
1.6. 
HRM Division will undertake a prior assessment of available cadre strength in a 
designaƟon vis-à-vis sancƟoned strength and publish oﬃce wise list of post, it intends 
to ﬁll up and posts likely to be vacant. PublicaƟon of list in advance would enable a 
Commissioner to make an informed choice so that he doesn’t opt for a choice of post 
which is likely to be not ﬁlled (blocked). 
1.7. 
All posts are divided into SensiƟve and Non-SensiƟve as per CVC guidelines of 1999 (as 
amended from Ɵme to Ɵme). The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines on 
tenure for, and rotaƟon on sensiƟve posts shall be strictly observed by the Competent 
Authority. 
1.8. 
Place of posƟng of an oﬃcial will be called Duty Oﬃce. Duty Oﬃce is an independent 
posƟng unit like Regional Oﬃce, District Oﬃce, Zonal Oﬃce, Head Oﬃce, Training 
Centre.  
1.9. 
All posƟngs are divided into “Field” and “Non-Field” posƟngs. PosƟngs in Regional, 
District Oﬃces and Special State Oﬃces in the ﬁeld shall be treated as “Field” posƟngs.

PosƟngs in the Head Oﬃce, Zonal Oﬃce, PDUNASS, the Zonal Training InsƟtute, the 
Sub-Zonal Training InsƟtute, NaƟonal Data Centre shall be treated as “Non-Field” 
posƟngs. The ACC as OIC of Zonal Oﬃce will be a ﬁeld posƟng.  
1.10. Composite Transfer Grant, Joining Time and other beneﬁts pursuant to request 
transfer shall not be admissible, in cases where request for transfer is made and the 
same is allowed in less than 2 years of conƟnuous service in any post. In case where 
such transfer is made aŌer 2 years of conƟnuous service in a post then Composite 
Transfer Grant, Joining Time and other beneﬁts shall be given. 
1.11. The provisions contained from clause 3 to clause 6 shall not apply to transfer/posƟng 
of ACC (HQ). The transfers/ posƟng of ACC (HQ) shall be done as per administraƟve 
requirement.

2.4.

order any transfer to meet administraƟve exigencies or on compassionate grounds. 
3. Types of Transfers & Placements 
All transfers and posƟng are categorised into following two types: 
(i) 
Transfers & Placement as part of AGT (Annual General Transfer) 
(ii) 
Non-AGT transfers and placements.  
 AGT is deﬁned as once-a-year annual exercise of transfer and placement of rotaƟonal 
cases, request cases and other cases. During the exercise, tenure and placement of 
oﬃcers is examined. Apart from those whose tenure is completed, other request cases 
shall also be taken-up and dealt.

3.1. Transfers & Placements as part of AGT 
This would consist following: 
 RotaƟonal Transfers: Oﬃcers who have compleƟng their tenure at Duty Oﬃce, StaƟon 
or Zone 
 Transfer on Request: Oﬃcers who have made request.  
 Transfer on PromoƟon: For oﬃcers RPFC-I and below wherein AGT is due within 04 
months of promoƟon.   
3.2. Non-AGT Transfers and Placements 
 IniƟal PosƟng on appointment  
 PosƟng on return from deputaƟon/ long-term training/ study leave 
 Transfer & PosƟng on PromoƟon (For grades Addl CPFC & above & other promoƟons 
where AGT is not due within 04 months of promoƟon) 
 Transfer on Request (Other than those during AGT)

4.1. 
In cases wherein an oﬃcer has completed minimum conƟnuous posƟng of two years at 
a duty oﬃce and makes a request for transfer, the tenure can be deemed completed and 
request may be dealt at par with other AGT cases.  
4.2. 
Security of minimum tenure (current tenure) at a duty oﬃce would have primacy over 
maximum conƟnuous tenure limits in Zone or at staƟon. IllustraƟon:  A Commissioner 
having not completed 09/12 years in a zone/ staƟon has been posted in the Zone/staƟon, 
then his that tenure at duty oﬃce shall be allowed to be completed, irrespecƟve 
maximum zonal tenure or staƟon tenure limit gets crossed mid-way unless he makes a 
request for transfer mid-tenure.  
4.3. 
Head Oﬃce & PDUNASS combined would be considered as a separate zone for all 
transfer purposes and Head Oﬃce-PDUNASS tenures would not be counted against Delhi 
NCR tenure limits. ZTI tenure would not be counted against Zonal tenures. 
4.4. 
All periods spent on deputaƟon, foreign assignment or study leave shall not be counted 
for the purpose of tenure.

5.2. 
Barring extraordinary circumstances with approval of Chairman CBT, no AGT transfer 
order shall be issued beyond 30th April of concerned AGT cycle. In case of any order

6. Rules & Principles governing transfers in AGT 
6.1. 
AGT transfers would consist of rotaƟonal transfers, transfer on request and transfers due 
on promoƟon within 04 months of AGT for RPFC-I and below. 
6.2. 
Record Date under this policy for calculaƟon of service and eligibility shall be 1st May of 
the Transfer Year (AGT Cycle Year). Date of joining would be taken as the basis for 
calculaƟon of service/ tenure on record date.  However, in case of delay in joining beyond 
30th April, for upto 30 more days, cases would be decided by HRM on case-to-case basis.  
6.3. 
Minimum prescribed tenure is three years on record date of AGT year. However, a 
Commissioner can be transferred before compleƟon of minimum prescribed tenure on 
his own request subject to recommendaƟon of CTPC or on administraƟve ground. 
6.4. 
All Commissioners would to be rotated between “Field” and “Non-Field” posƟng 
regularly. The principles of rotaƟons shall be as follows: 
 
i. 
No conƟnuous two “Field posƟngs” can be allowed for commissioners in RPFC-
I and above designaƟon. However, in case of non-availability of suﬃcient 
oﬃcers for rotaƟon, or for any other suﬃcient administraƟve requirements, 
such conƟnuous posƟngs may be recommended by the CTPC. While making 
such recommendaƟon, CTPC shall give preference to oﬃcers with lower tenure 
in ﬁeld posƟngs in that designaƟon. 
ii. 
Normally only 2 conƟnuous “Field posƟngs” can be allowed for commissioners 
in RPFC-II designaƟon. In case, enough posts are not available under Non-ﬁeld 
posƟng then those with the maximum Non-ﬁeld posƟng in the same

designaƟon shall be considered for third conƟnuous Field posƟng. But in no case 
RPFC-II can be OIC for two conƟnuous terms. 
iii. 
ConƟnuous “ﬁeld posƟngs” may be allowed for commissioners in APFC grade 
provided they are not made OICs conƟnuously. 
iv. 
However, alternate Field and Non-Field posƟngs may be allowed to all oﬃcers 
in diﬀerent oﬃces at the same staƟon. 
v. 
No two tenures shall be allowed at any duty oﬃce as OIC.  
6.5. 
PosƟng on PromoƟon 
6.5.1. If promoƟon is due within one year, then as far as feasible, an oﬃcer will not be 
transferred. However, when an oﬃcer is transferred and then promoted and due for 
transfer then he may be either retained at that staƟon, or if that is not feasible then in 
accordance with his choices as provided in 6.5.2 be considered.   
6.5.2. Transfer from duty oﬃce shall be mandatory upon PromoƟon.  Oﬃcer (s) promoted 
within 04 months of AGT due, shall be transferred as per process of AGT. In case AGT is 
not due within 04 months, such oﬃcers aŌer promoƟon may give their opƟons through 
oﬃcial email to HRM.  
6.5.3. On promoƟon from Group B to Group A, there shall be compulsory transfer from parent 
Zone/State (whichever is larger). As far as possible, Group B oﬃcers promoted to Group 
A and opƟng for their parent Zone for subsequent sƟnts can be posted in their parent 
Zone of Group B in those oﬃces in which they have not served as EO or have served 
minimum. 
6.6. 
Transfer on Request 
6.6.1. Transfer Requests shall normally be considered at the Ɵme of Annual General Transfers 
(AGT) along with Annual RotaƟonal Transfers.  
6.6.2. All Commissioners can request for premature transfer during AGT.  Other Transfer on 
Request outside AGT would be dealt on case-to-case basis. 
6.6.3. Among other things CTPC shall consider following while disposing Request Transfer cases 
in non-OIC posƟngs: 
a. PosƟng of spouses/ Persons with Disability etc: PosƟng of spouses and persons 
with Disability / Persons who are caregivers of Disabled Dependents etc. shall be 
regulated as per extant guidelines issued by DoPT, Government of India. 
b. Tenure of posƟng in North-Eastern Region (NER), Andaman & Nicobar Islands,

J&K and Ladakh shall be guided by the policy of Government of India on transfer 
and tenure for such places. Further any concessions granted by DOPT for any 
these posƟngs or other hard posƟngs would be applicable to oﬃcers of Central 
Board.  
c. The norms for transfer in respect of Oﬃcers due to reƟre within two years to the 
extent administraƟvely feasible shall be guided by the norms of DoP&T.  
6.7. 
Pre-mature Transfers & Transfers on AdministraƟve Grounds  
a. In case of an administraƟve exigency, the Chairman CBT may transfer a 
Commissioner without the recommendaƟon of CTPC. 
b. Any order for premature transfer shall be done by the Chairman CBT. 
c. CPFC may eﬀect transfer on promoƟon upto Addl. CPFC outside AGT for 
administraƟve requirement with approval of Chairman, CBT. 
6.8. 
Transfer on compleƟon of hard posƟng: Once a Commissioner has completed hard 
posƟng tenure and give opƟon for his transfer, as far as feasible, his choices shall be 
accommodated.   
6.9. 
PosƟng on return from deputaƟon/ long-term training/ study leave 
The oﬃcer returning from deputaƟon/ long-term-training/study leave will join Zonal 
Oﬃce under which jurisdicƟon, he was posted earlier before going for deputaƟon/ long-
term training/ study leave. In case required, addiƟonal post may be operated by the 
Head Oﬃce. In case of his posƟng in HO and PDUNASS/ZTI, he will report to HO and 
PDUNASS/ZTIs respecƟvely.  
6.10. DeputaƟon 
External DeputaƟon shall be allowed aŌer 9 years of service under Central Board except it 
can be allowed aŌer 06 years’ service on spouse grounds. Internal DeputaƟon shall be 
allowed aŌer 05 years of service. DeputaƟon is intended to provide best pracƟce exposure 
to EPFO Commissioners, personality development and exposure to challenging 
environments parƟcularly in target areas of Data Center Management, RegulaƟon, 
Investment, Enforcement, Finance, AdministraƟon and Customer Service Delivery. 
DeputaƟon shall not be denied normally if shortage in the designaƟon is not more than 30% 
of the sancƟoned posts.  
7. General Principles & Procedures 
7.1. 
Based on number of available oﬃcers and vacancies and aŌer assessing workload HR

will earmark grade-wise posts that will remain under AddiƟonal Charge.  
7.2. 
Before opƟons for AGT are called, HRM will undertake the following pre- AGT 
assessment and freeze the informaƟon: 
a. IdenƟfy posts wherein transfers will be made and/or are currently vacant and are 
not in blocked posts category. 
b. IdenƟfy posts that are under zone of consideraƟon of transfer as based on the 
norms laid down. 
c. Prepare a tentaƟve list of oﬃcers who would be under consideraƟon of AGT as 
per TP-CC 2025 norms. 
d. Develop a list of posts available for transfers from the above set of informaƟon. 
Further, oversee a IT tool which supports categorizaƟon of each post as per 
Nature (Field/ Non-Field), (ii) SensiƟvity (Vigilance Angle) 
7.3. 
Total of ﬁve staƟon opƟon shall be called from an oﬃcer. These opƟons shall be received 
through online-IT tool.   
7.4. 
CTPC will list all the ﬁrst opƟons on the matrix of oﬃces. Further, following as guiding 
principle is laid out for CTPC for recommending transfer: 
i. 
If number of eligible opƟons is lower than or equal to vacancy, CTPC may 
ordinarily recommend based on opƟon exercised.  
ii. 
For non-ﬁeld oﬃces, ﬁrst preference to DOPT norms covered cases then to those 
who have served least in non-ﬁeld oﬃces cumulaƟvely and then least in non-ﬁeld 
in that Zone/State/Region (larger to smaller) in that order.  
iii. For the ﬁeld oﬃces at OIC posts, ﬁrst priority to an otherwise eligible 
Commissioner who has served least period as an OIC in that designaƟon and then 
least period as OIC in designaƟons below thereaŌer served period in that 
State/Zone/Region (larger to smaller) in that order. 
iv. For the ﬁeld oﬃces at Non OIC posts, ﬁrst priority to Request Transfers as per 
DOPT guidelines/ rules/ norms and if no reasonable request, then to a 
commissioner having least total ﬁeld service and thereaŌer least ﬁeld service in 
that Zone/State/Region (larger to smaller) in that order. 
7.5. 
Each AGT shall consist of two lists of transferees: (a) oﬃcers who are being transferred 
based on AGT norms and list of cases which are in deviaƟon of the norm. These lists 
would further indicate cases done on request ground.

8. Grievance Redressal Mechanism  
8.1. 
Every Commissioner aggrieved by an order of transfer has a right to make applicaƟon 
before the Competent Authority within ﬁve days of issue of such order. 
8.2. 
Grievance from a Commissioners whose request for transfer is not heeded can also make 
such a request. 
8.3. 
All such grievances shall be received and disposed online through HR SoŌ portal as 
prescribed schedule. Till the disposal of grievance, oﬃcer may not be relieved. If 
“incoming oﬃcer” has been relieved and joined then “outgoing oﬃcer” may get aƩached 
to nearest non-ﬁeld oﬃce (distance wise) Ɵll disposal of grievance. 
8.4. 
HRM Division shall refer all such grievances to Grievance CommiƩee. In case it requires 
to take view of any other Commissioner who may be aﬀected owing to such request, 
then their viewpoint may also be considered by the CommiƩee (GRC) 
8.5. 
The Grievance Redressal CommiƩee shall examine grievances on case-to-case basis and 
forward its recommendaƟons to the Competent Authority.  
8.6. 
The Competent Authority shall dispose the grievances and such disposal shall be 
communicated to the concerned Commissioner through HR SoŌ or any other prescribed 
mode. 
9. Miscellaneous  
9.1. 
All subsequent amendments to the Transfer Policy shall be incorporated in this Policy 
and a consolidated Transfer Policy shall be duly published on the web site. 
9.2. 
ACC(HR) shall serve as nodal oﬃcer and shall be responsible to iniƟate the process of 
AGT as per Ɵmelines. The Nodal oﬃcer shall also be charge with the duty of seeking 
views of stakeholders regarding diﬃculƟes faced by them under or improvement to be 
made to this Policy and to compile and process them further. 
9.3. 
ResidenƟal / leased AccommodaƟon of the Board: Any transfer ordered in public interest 
beyond the schedule prescribed shall enƟtle the oﬃcer for the conƟnued retenƟon of 
the residenƟal accommodaƟon owned by the Board Ɵll the end of the ﬁnancial year in 
which such transfer is ordered or Ɵll the period prescribed under Residence Rules 
applicable for the oﬃcers and the employees of the Board, whichever is later. Under 
excepƟonal circumstances relaxaƟon to retain accommodaƟon can be given by the 
Competent Authority. The rule relaƟng to retenƟon of leased accommodaƟon shall be 
applied as prescribed.

9.4. 
Transfers on administraƟve grounds 
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Transfer Policy, the Competent Authority may eﬀect 
transfer of any oﬃcial any Ɵme on administraƟve requirements anywhere in the Country.   
10. 
Power to remove diﬃculƟes 
10.1. In case of any doubt regarding any of the provisions of the TP-CC 2025, the maƩer shall 
be placed before CPFC for consideraƟon. The decision of CPFC shall be ﬁnal in regard to 
maƩers thus referred. The same shall be placed before the Chairman, CBT for 
informaƟon. 
10.2. In case of any diﬃculty in the implementaƟon of the Policy that may be noƟced, 
amendments may be recommended in the TP-CC 2025 and placed before the Chairman, 
CBT for approval. Each such amendment of the Policy along with a consolidated Transfer 
Policy, aŌer incorporaƟng such changes, shall be formally noƟﬁed and shall also be 
placed in the public domain.
